- We don't fully understand *why* measurement works this way, but that's a physics problem, not a consciousness problem

- Von Neumann and Wigner (1930s pioneers) did speculatively link consciousness to collapse, but this was fringe even then
- Pop-science books exaggerated this into common knowledge
- It's philosophically *interesting*, which makes it sticky

**The actual state of play:**
- Most working physicists use interpretations (many-worlds, decoherence, pilot-wave) that don't invoke consciousness at all
- Experiments work identically whether or not anyone is "observing"
- No experiment has ever shown consciousness affects quantum outcomes
